title: Meadows Row
summary: A one-arm landmine row, done standing side-on to the bar, that gives the lats a long stretch at the bottom.

equipment_needs.text: Needs: landmine attachment; barbell (Olympic bar); weight plates.

muscles.why: Library rating 1 for lats (main mover): each working set adds 1 of a set to the weekly lats total.
Library rating 0.8 for upper back (main mover): each working set adds 0.8 of a set to the weekly upper back total.
Library rating 0.5 for rear delts (helper): each working set adds 0.5 of a set to the weekly rear delts total.
Library rating 0.5 for traps (helper): each working set adds 0.5 of a set to the weekly traps total.
Library rating 0.5 for biceps (helper): each working set adds 0.5 of a set to the weekly biceps total.
Library rating 0.4 for forearms (helper): each working set adds 0.4 of a set to the weekly forearms total.
Library rating 0.2 for lower back: below the counting floor, so it adds nothing to the weekly lower back total.

setup.text: Stand side-on to the end of a landmine bar in a staggered stance and grip the thick end overhand.
Rest your free forearm on your front knee and let the bar hang so your lat stretches.
Row your elbow up and back toward your hip.
Lower slowly to the full stretch.

form_cues.cue: Brace the free forearm on your knee
Row the elbow up and back
Use straps if your grip gives out first. The bar end is thick.

mistakes.text: Twisting the torso to finish the rep.

lower_risk.text: Warm-up: the app adds up to 2 ramp-up sets only when the load is heavy for the equipment and the main muscle is not warm yet.
The app suggests a heavier load only when the jump is 7.5% or less; otherwise it adds a rep first.
Default target: 8-12 reps, stopping about 3 reps short of failure (RIR 3). Stop the set when form breaks down.
Use the same controlled range on every rep; lower under control rather than dropping or bouncing.
Pick a variation and range you can train pain-free.
